They compare this novel metric to the standard 95–95–95 targets, demonstrating how traditional indicators may obscure the true distribution of viraemia and thus mislead prevention priorities. The study rigorously evaluates the performance of different metrics in predicting transmission risk and identifies limitations in current surveillance approaches. This focus on methodological design, model selection, bias correction, and evaluation of surveillance metrics aligns precisely with Class 5. Multi-step inference questions could explore how model assumptions affect burden estimates, how different metrics perform under varying population structures, or how measurement error in viral load testing might influence the viraemia profile—requiring integration of epidemiological principles with statistical reasoning.
